key: Cut down the whole forest (of lust), not a tree only! Danger comes out of the forest (of lust).
s: Between verses on zeal and love’s bond, the chapter speaks to the Bhikshus; the Theravāda commentary, on verse 283, hears ‘not a tree’ as the Teacher checking new monks who took him to mean trees, since he meant the forest of defilements such as lust.

evidence.words: Tattha mā rukkhanti satthārā hi ‘‘vanaṃ chindathā’’ti vutte tesaṃ acirapabbajitānaṃ ‘‘satthā amhe vāsiādīni gahetvā vanaṃ chindāpetī’’ti rukkhaṃ chinditukāmatā uppajji. Atha ne ‘‘mayā rāgādikilesavanaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ, na rukkhe’’ti paṭisedhento ‘‘mā rukkha’’nti āha.
evidence.gloss: ‘Not a tree’: when the Teacher said ‘Cut down the forest’, a wish to cut trees arose in those recently ordained monks, who thought ‘the Teacher is having us take adzes and the like and cut down the forest’; then, checking them with ‘I said this with reference to the forest of defilements such as lust, not to trees’, he said ‘not a tree’.
